title: Run
description: One evaluation of one resource, exactly as the engine emits it today. This describes `Run.to_dict()` and nothing more: where the current output is awkward, the awkwardness is documented rather than corrected, because a schema that describes what the code should do cannot validate what it does. Normalisation is a later, deliberate step with its own compatibility decision.

provenance.description: Carried through from the evidence document unchanged. Owned by the evidence schema; not restated here, so that one definition moves at a time.

coverage.description: Also from the evidence. Note the name: a RunSet calls the same idea `run_coverage`, and the two envelopes disagree. Recorded, not fixed.

resource.description: The full resource block from the evidence, with display name and url. Each result inside carries a narrower copy holding only id and type.

resource_class.description: A label, never a filter. `unknown` is the ordinary value: today only lists are classified.

class_reason.description: Why the class is what it is, including why it is `unknown`.

set_aside.description: Whether this resource was set aside rather than evaluated.

rule_source.description: Which rules evaluated this, in words rather than a path. A free string today.

$schema.description: The exact contract this document claims, which must be the $id of the schema validating it. An instance convention and not the dialect keyword: inside a schema document `$schema` names the JSON Schema dialect, and using one field for both meanings is what this separation exists to prevent. It replaces `schema_version`, which was a second version that could not even express the one in the $id — `1.0` against a contract ending in `/1.2.0` — and was maintained by hand.

counts.description: One key per outcome, always all six, zeros included. A count that disappears when it is zero makes an absent key and a zero look the same.

outcome.description: Six values as emitted, and the product speaks of five. `error` is the sixth and it is not a governance answer: it says the evaluation itself failed, which is a different sentence from anything the tenant did. Recorded here because the engine emits it.

rule_version.description: The version of the rule as it was evaluated. This is what makes a later comparison able to say `rule-version` moved rather than reporting it as tenant drift.

schema_version.description: The rule schema's version. Note what is missing: the Run document itself carries no version at the top level, only each result does, so a stored run cannot be versioned as a document. An imperfection, described rather than repaired.

message.description: What the outcome means, in a sentence a person reads.

basis.description: The rule's basis type as a bare string: requirement, documented-limit, documented-guidance or convention. An opinion is not one.

evidence_used.description: Every fact the rule read, present or absent, with the bounds where the value was not exact. This is what makes a finding re-checkable, and it is why an assessment keeps its evidence whole.

passes_without_resolving.description: What a pass does NOT settle. Present on every result, including failing ones.

sources.description: The rule's normative sources. Empty for a convention, which is the honest value rather than an omission.

message_degraded.description: Whether the message had to fall back because the rule could not phrase its own.

engine_detail.description: Why the engine could not do what the rule asked. Empty when nothing went wrong, which is the ordinary case.

evidenceUsed.description: All six keys always present, with nulls rather than omissions. An absent key and a null mean different things, and emitting both would make them indistinguishable.

state.description: The evidence state: observed, missing, not-supported, permission-denied, partial or invalid.

value.description: The exact value where one was observed, and null where it was not. Any JSON type, because a fact can be a number, a string, a boolean or a list.

lower_bound.description: Set where the value is known to be at least this, which is how a partial expansion still decides a rule.

upper_bound.description: Set where the value is known to be at most this.

detail.description: Why the fact is in the state it is in.
